title.narrative: UNDP Promoting Biodiversity and Ecosystem-Based Adaptation to Climate Change in Wadi Gaza Coastal Wetland

description.narrative:
Support to componets related to: Biodiversity Museum, Development of New Wadi Gaza Waterway and Flood Protection, Cleaning & Naturalization of Wadi Gaza (All cleaning works, Part of Greening)
Protecting natural resources and safeguarding the environment. The project aims to protect public health of the Gaza Strip and its natural resources through restoration and rehabilitation of Wadi Gaza as a recognized natural reserve and coastal wetland. The project will enhance the livelihood of residents of surrounding towns though development of recreational facilities and creating job opportunities through the planned project activities.
Wadi Gaza is a vibrant and diverse biological environment with a total area estimated at 200 hectares. The wadi (valley), besides serving as a stopover for many migratory birds, has the potential for becoming a recreational area for the local population and a tourist attraction. The area is home to 158 terrestrial vertebrate fauna species (17 mammals, 120 birds, 18 reptiles, and 3 amphibians) as well as 120 birds belonging to 12 orders, 40 families, and 84 genera as well as 250 species of vascular plants.
The restoration of Wadi Gaza is expected to reduce the vulnerability of ecosystems to extreme events and slow-onset changes. The adaptation benefits associated with greening, flood risk mitigation, improving natural water storage capacities, can help ameliorate the impact of droughts, reduce soil erosion, as well as improve and diversify livelihoods for the most vulnerable groups of population. Greening Wadi Gaza will contribute to climate mitigation by increasing the absorption capacity of CO2 equivalent.
